aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abel-2.title: Abel
abel-2.note: Not Cain's brother. In these two verses Abel is a place: the great stone of Abel in a Beth-shemite's field where the ark came to rest, and a short form of the northern city people went to for good advice.

abiathar.title: Abiathar
abiathar.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
abiathar.note: He was the only priest to get out of Nob alive when Saul had the place killed, and he went straight to David and stayed his priest through the running years and the reign. At the end he backed Adonijah instead of Solomon, and Solomon sent him away from the priesthood rather than kill him.

abiel-2.title: Abiel
abiel-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abiel-2.note: Kish's father, which makes him Saul's grandfather. One of David's warriors carried the name as well. Nothing connects the two men but the spelling.

abigal.title: Abigal
abigal.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
abigal.note: A variant spelling of Abigail, David's wife. She rode out to stop David wiping out her first husband Nabal's household, and it worked. Once Nabal was dead she married David.

abijah-2.title: Abijah
abijah-2.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
abijah-2.note: A levite from the united kingdom. 1 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice.

abinadab-3.title: Abinadab
abinadab-3.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-3.note: One of David's older brothers, named in the family lists and not much else.

abinadab.title: Abinadab
abinadab.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab.note: A son of Saul, who died alongside his father.

abinadab-2.title: Abinadab
abinadab-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-2.note: The man whose house held the ark. It sat there twenty years before David came for it.

abishai.title: Abishai
abishai.about: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abishai.note: David's nephew, and the most willing man he had. He is credited with three hundred killed on his own. Twice he offered to finish one of David's enemies on the spot, Saul asleep in the camp and Shimei cursing on the road, and both times David told him no.

abner.title: Abner
abner.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
abner.note: Saul's cousin, and the commander of his army. When Saul died he did not stop: he kept the war going between David and what was left of Saul's house.

achish.title: Achish
achish.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
achish.note: He is the Philistine king of Gath, and he took David in while David was running from Saul.

adriel.title: Adriel
adriel.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adriel.note: Saul had promised his elder daughter Merab to David, then gave her to Adriel instead. Their five sons were later handed over to the Gibeonites.

adullam.title: Adullam
adullam.note: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.

agag.title: Agag
agag.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
agag.note: King of the Amalekites. Saul was told to destroy him and his people completely. He spared Agag and the best of the livestock, and that disobedience cost him God's favour.

ahiah-2.title: Ahiah
ahiah-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahiah-2.note: The priest with Saul at Michmash, carrying the ephod when Saul asked whether to go into the battle. He is a son of Ahitub, and the same man the lists elsewhere call Ahimelech.

ahimaaz-3.title: Ahimaaz
ahimaaz-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimaaz-3.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

ahimelech.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech.note: The priest at Nob. He helped David, who was fleeing Saul, without knowing it, and gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Once Doeg reported it, Saul had him and the rest of the priests at Nob massacred.

ahimelech-3.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech-3.note: One of 3 men called Ahimelech. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Samuel.

ahinoam.title: Ahinoam
ahinoam.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinoam.note: The Ahinoam from Jezreel whom David married, mother of his firstborn son Amnon, and a different woman from Saul's wife of the same name.

ahinoam-2.title: Ahinoam
ahinoam-2.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinoam-2.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a woman from the united kingdom.

ahitub.title: Ahitub
ahitub.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahitub.note: Ahimelech's father, in Israel's high priestly line.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

aphek.title: Aphek
aphek.note: The Philistines captured the ark of the covenant from Israel at Aphek. A later battle there went the other way, when Israel beat the Arameans after Elisha promised King Jehoash the victory.

aphiah.title: Aphiah
aphiah.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
aphiah.note: One of Saul's ancestors, named in the opening line of his genealogy and nowhere else.

aroer-3.title: Aroer
aroer-3.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

ashdod.title: Ashdod
ashdod.note: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.

ashkelon.title: Ashkelon
ashkelon.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.

ashtoreth.title: Ashtoreth
ashtoreth.about: A female deity in the Old Testament
ashtoreth.note: A Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely tied to Baal worship. Solomon built her a shrine late in his reign to please a foreign wife, and that is given as a main reason the kingdom split.

athach.title: Athach
athach.note: David sent it a share of the spoil he took back from the Amalekite raiders who hit Ziklag, a gift to the elders of Judah who had put up with him in his outlaw years. The name occurs nowhere else, and some suggest a copyist's slip for Ether.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

bechorath.title: Bechorath
bechorath.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
bechorath.note: Saul's family tree runs through him: son of Aphiah, an early forebear of Kish, Saul's father. The genealogy is there to set out Saul's Benjamite pedigree just before he comes on stage.

bedan.title: Bedan
bedan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
bedan.note: Samuel names him in his farewell speech among Israel's deliverers, with Jerubbaal, Barak and Jephthah. No judge called Bedan appears in the book of Judges, so who he was is uncertain.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

besor.title: Besor
besor.note: A brook in southern Judah. Two hundred of David's men were too worn out to cross it and stayed behind while the rest chased the Amalekite raiders. David then insisted that the men who stayed with the supplies share the spoil equally.

beth-aven.title: Beth-aven
beth-aven.note: House of vanity. It lay in the hill country of Benjamin near Ai and Bethel, served as a boundary marker in Joshua, and was where Israel's forces gathered before Jonathan's fight with the Philistines in 1 Samuel 14.

beth-car.title: Beth-car
beth-car.note: It lay west of Mizpah, the point Israel chased the Philistines to after Samuel's victory. It was the same battle after which the stone Ebenezer went up.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-el-2.title: Beth-el
beth-el-2.note: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

beth-shean.title: Beth-shean
beth-shean.note: After Saul died on Gilboa, the Philistines hung his body and his sons' bodies on the walls of this city. Beth-shean was Canaanite, in Manasseh's land. It stood where the Jezreel and Jordan valleys meet.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bethlehemite.title: Bethlehemite
bethlehemite.note: Someone from Bethlehem, which is how Scripture introduces Jesse and his son David before either needed a longer introduction.

bethshemite.title: Bethshemite
bethshemite.note: Someone from Beth-shemesh, a town of Judah near the Philistine border. When the Philistines sent the ark of the covenant back on a cart, it came to rest in a Bethshemite's field.

bezek-2.title: Bezek
bezek-2.note: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

bozez.title: Bozez
bozez.note: It is a rock, not a man. Bozez and Seneh were the two crags on either side of the pass where Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed up to surprise the Philistine garrison at Michmash.

caleb.title: Caleb
caleb.about: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
caleb.note: One of the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan. He and Joshua were the only two who came back telling Israel to trust God and take the land, and the rest of that generation paid for ignoring them with forty years in the wilderness.

carmel.title: Carmel
carmel.note: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal happened on this mountain ridge on Israel's Mediterranean coast. Fire came down from heaven when Elijah prayed, and Baal had nothing to answer with.

carmelite.title: Carmelite
carmelite.note: Here it means someone from Carmel in Judah's hill country, not Mount Carmel in the north. Nabal was a Carmelite, the rich fool who insulted David, and so was his wife Abigail, who married David after Nabal died.

cherethims-2.title: Cherethims
cherethims-2.note: The people themselves, close neighbours of the Philistines and likely from Crete. Ezekiel and Zephaniah both name them in oracles of judgment.

chorashan.title: Chorashan
chorashan.note: After he rescued the Ziklag captives from the Amalekites, David sent gifts from the plunder to a string of towns, and this was one. It is generally identified with Ashan, a town of Simeon in the Negev of Judah.

dagon.title: Dagon
dagon.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
dagon.note: The Philistines set the captured ark in Dagon's temple at Ashdod. His statue was found face down before the ark, and the second time it had lost its head and hands.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

doeg.title: Doeg
doeg.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
doeg.note: Saul's chief herdsman, an Edomite, who told Saul that the priest Ahimelech had helped David. Saul's own men would not kill the priests of Nob. Doeg did it himself, eighty-five priests and the whole town with them.

ebenezer.title: Ebenezer
ebenezer.note: Stone of help. The Philistines first beat Israel near here and took the ark. Years later, after a win over the Philistines in the same area, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen and gave it that name for the Lord's help.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

edomite.title: Edomite
edomite.note: Esau's descendants, living in Seir south and east of the Dead Sea. Kin to Israel and at odds with it for most of the record. Egyptian texts mention Edom as early as the thirteenth century BC, and its capital Busayra and the copper works at Khirbat en Nahas have both been excavated.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

ekronite.title: Ekronite
ekronite.note: Somebody from Ekron. When the ark arrived after the plagues at Ashdod and Gath, the Ekronites cried out in terror and demanded it go back to Israel.

elah.title: Elah
elah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elah.note: David killed Goliath in the Valley of Elah, the terebinth valley in Judah's lowlands, with the two armies on opposite slopes. The name also belongs to Elah son of Baasha, king of Israel, murdered while drunk by Zimri, his own chariot commander. Khirbet Qeiyafa above the valley has a tenth century BC fort and one of the earliest Hebrew inscriptions.

eleazar-4.title: Eleazar
eleazar-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
eleazar-4.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 1 Samuel is the only book that names him.

eli.title: Eli
eli.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
eli.note: The high priest and judge at Shiloh who raised Samuel after Hannah gave him to the Lord. His sons stole sacrificial meat and slept with the women serving at the tabernacle door, and Eli only scolded them. Both died in the battle where the ark was taken, and Eli fell backward off his seat at the news and broke his neck, aged ninety-eight.

eliab-2.title: Eliab
eliab-2.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
eliab-2.note: David's eldest brother. He was tall and looked the part, and Samuel thought he was the one until God told him the Lord looks at the heart. Later he tore into David for turning up at the Goliath battle line.

elihu-5.title: Elihu
elihu-5.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
elihu-5.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a Levite from the united kingdom.

elkanah.title: Elkanah
elkanah.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
elkanah.note: Samuel's father. He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and loved Hannah though she had no children and Peninnah taunted her for it. That is where Hannah's prayer for a son starts.

en-dor.title: En-dor
en-dor.note: Home of the medium Saul went to in disguise the night before his last battle. It lay in Issachar's land, near where Deborah and Barak beat Sisera. Endur, southeast of Mount Tabor, keeps the name.

en-gedi.title: En-gedi
en-gedi.note: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, fed by a spring that drops some 600 feet down the cliffs. David hid in its caves from Saul and spared Saul's life there. A Chalcolithic temple on the site is far older than Israel in Canaan.

ephes-dammim.title: Ephes-dammim
ephes-dammim.note: The Philistines camped here in the Valley of Elah when Goliath came out and David killed him. Chronicles calls it Pas-dammim, and it is generally placed near Socoh in the Shephelah.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ephraimite.title: Ephraimite
ephraimite.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraimite.note: Someone of the tribe of Ephraim. In Judges 12 the men of Gilead caught Ephraimites at the fords by making them say shibboleth, and killed those who could not get the first sound right.

ephraimite-2.title: Ephraimite
ephraimite-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ephraimite-2.note: Ruth and 1 Samuel name him twice, and he is a woman from the wilderness years.

eshtemoa.title: Eshtemoa
eshtemoa.note: David sent some of the Amalekite plunder to the elders of Eshtemoa, a priestly town south of Hebron, for standing by him in his outlaw years. It survives as es-Samu, where old ruins have been found.

ezel.title: Ezel
ezel.note: A stone near Saul's house at Gibeah where David hid while Jonathan found out what his father meant to do. It was the last time the two met before David fled for good.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gad-2.title: Gad
gad-2.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
gad-2.note: A prophet of the united monarchy, and nothing to do with Jacob's son. He first turns up in 1 Samuel 22:5, comes back in 2 Samuel 24, and Chronicles names him again.

gallim.title: Gallim
gallim.note: Michal was given to Palti of Gallim after Saul took her away from David. Isaiah lists the town, in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, among the places panicking as the Assyrian army comes on.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

geshuri.title: Geshuri
geshuri.note: David married Maacah, daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur, and so these people were Absalom's family on his mother's side. Their small Aramean kingdom lay east of the Sea of Galilee.

gezrites.title: Gezrites
gezrites.note: David raided them from Ziklag along with the Geshurites and Amalekites. Most read the name as Girzites, an otherwise unknown desert tribe in the Negev toward Egypt, and not the people of Gezer.

gilboa.title: Gilboa
gilboa.note: Saul died on these hills above the Jezreel Valley. The Philistines broke his army, three of his sons fell, Jonathan among them, and Saul, badly wounded, took his own life. David's lament curses Gilboa never to have dew or rain.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

goliath.title: Goliath
goliath.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
goliath.note: The Philistine champion from Gath whom the young David killed in the valley of Elah. The traditional Hebrew text makes him over nine feet, while the Dead Sea Scrolls and the earliest Greek give about six foot nine. One later passage credits Elhanan, and Chronicles makes Elhanan's man Goliath's brother.

hachilah.title: Hachilah
hachilah.note: David hid from Saul on this hill in the wilderness. From here he and Abishai crept into Saul's camp at night and took his spear and water jug instead of killing him.

hannah.title: Hannah
hannah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
hannah.note: Elkanah loved her, and she had no children, and his other wife Peninnah made sure she felt it. She prayed so hard and so silently at Shiloh that Eli thought she was drunk. Samuel was the answer, and she gave him to the Lord's service once he was weaned.

havilah-3.title: Havilah
havilah-3.note: Genesis puts it near the rivers of Eden and calls it rich in gold. The name turns up in two different family lines, so it may be two places.

hazor.title: Hazor
hazor.note: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

hereth.title: Hereth
hereth.note: A forest in Judah. David hid there with his growing band after leaving his parents with the king of Moab, and the prophet Gad told him to go. Where it was is unknown.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hophni.title: Hophni
hophni.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
hophni.note: Eli's son, a priest at Shiloh, and a corrupt one. He and his brother Phinehas died in the battle where the Philistines took the Ark.

hormah.title: Hormah
hormah.note: Its name means "devoted to destruction", and it was first called Zephath. Israel was beaten there after going into Canaan without the Lord, following the spies' report. Later Israel vowed to destroy the cities of the region, and the vow, kept under Joshua, gave the town its name.

i-chabod.title: I-chabod
i-chabod.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
i-chabod.note: His mother named him as she died giving birth, having just heard that the ark was taken and that her husband Phinehas and his father Eli were both dead. The name means "no glory".

ishuai-2.title: Ishuai
ishuai-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ishuai-2.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jattir.title: Jattir
jattir.note: A priests' town in the hill country of Judah, given to Aaron's line. David sent its elders a share of the Amalekite plunder, as he did for many towns while he was on the run. It is identified with Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron.

jehoshua-3.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshua-3.note: One of 4 men called Jehoshua. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named twice in 1 Samuel.

jephthah.title: Jephthah
jephthah.note: Son of a prostitute, thrown out by his half-brothers, and leading a gang of raiders when Gilead's elders came begging him to fight the Ammonites. He vowed to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first after the victory, and it was his daughter, his only child. Judges tells it without approving the vow or explaining why he kept it.

jerahmeelites.title: Jerahmeelites
jerahmeelites.note: A clan of Judah, Jerahmeel's people, living in the Negev. While David was based at Ziklag under Philistine protection he raided their country, and later he sent them a share of the Amalekite plunder as allies.

jeroham.title: Jeroham
jeroham.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
jeroham.note: Samuel's family line goes back through him: he was the prophet's great-grandfather's generation, in the genealogy that opens 1 Samuel and again in the Levitical lists of Chronicles.

jerubbaal.title: Jerubbaal
jerubbaal.note: "Let Baal contend." Gideon got the name after he pulled down his father's altar to Baal and nothing happened to him, so the name is a taunt at a god who could not answer.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jezreel-2.title: Jezreel
jezreel-2.note: Not the northern valley. This Jezreel is a town in the hill country near Hebron, listed in Joshua 15:56.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave Absalom. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jobesh-gilead.title: Jobesh
jobesh-gilead.note: Better known as Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Its men stayed home from the war against Benjamin and were nearly wiped out for it, and their daughters were handed to Benjamin's survivors as wives. When Nahash the Ammonite besieged it, Saul rescued it. Years later its men took his body down from the walls of Beth-shan and buried it.

joel.title: Joel
joel.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
joel.note: Samuel's son, and not the prophet. Chronicles puts him in the Levite lists, and he is the father in a line of temple singers.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

keilah.title: Keilah
keilah.note: David saved this walled town from a Philistine raid while Saul was hunting him. Then he learned they would have handed him over if Saul came, and he moved on into the wilderness of Ziph.

kenite.title: Kenite
kenite.note: They were a wandering clan close to Midian, outside the twelve tribes but mostly friendly to Israel. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, was a Kenite priest, and Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, killed Sisera.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

kish.title: Kish
kish.about: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy
kish.note: Saul's father, a Benjamite of some standing. He lost his donkeys, sent Saul to find them, and the search ended with Samuel anointing Saul as Israel's first king.

laish-2.title: Laish
laish-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
laish-2.note: 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

malchishua.title: Malchishua
malchishua.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
malchishua.note: One of Saul's sons, who died with his father and brothers when the Philistines beat Israel on Mount Gilboa.

maoch.title: Maoch
maoch.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
maoch.note: Father of Achish, the Philistine king of Gath who took David in when Saul was hunting him. A later king of Gath, Achish son of Maacah, turns up in Solomon's time, and whether Maoch and Maacah are the same man or the name just ran in that royal house is uncertain.

maon.title: Maon
maon.note: About seven miles south of Hebron, in the Judean hill country. David hid from Saul in the wilderness named after it, and Nabal, whose widow Abigail married David, kept his flocks there. The ruins, now Tell Ma'in, still mark the spot.

matri.title: Matri
matri.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
matri.note: When the lot fell on Saul to be Israel's first king, it fell first on his family within Benjamin, the Matri, and that is the only time they are named.

mecholathite.title: Mecholathite
mecholathite.note: Adriel's tag, the man Saul gave Merab to after promising her to David. It places him at Abel-meholah. His five sons by Merab were later handed to the Gibeonites and executed to end a famine brought on by Saul's violence against them.

merab.title: Merab
merab.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
merab.note: The elder of Saul's two daughters. Saul promised her to David after Goliath and then gave her to Adriel of Meholah instead. Her five sons by Adriel were later handed over to the Gibeonites and executed for Saul's slaughter of their people.

michal.title: Michal
michal.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michal.note: Saul's younger daughter. David won her by killing two hundred Philistines, and she saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul's men came. Saul then gave her to another man; David took her back as king, but she despised him for dancing before the ark, and she had no children to the end of her life.

migron.title: Migron
migron.note: Saul camped under a pomegranate tree at Migron, near Gibeah, with about six hundred men, just before Jonathan's raid on the Philistines at Michmash. Isaiah has an invading army pass a Migron near Aiath, apparently a different spot of the same name.

mikmas.title: Mikmas
mikmas.note: Michmash, a town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem. The Philistines gathered there against Saul, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer climbed across a rocky ravine to attack their garrison, which set off a rout. Isaiah pictures the Assyrian army leaving its baggage there, and families from Michmash came back from Babylon.

mitspah.title: Mitspah
mitspah.note: A watchtower name, which is why so many places carry it. This one is where Jacob and Laban piled stones and agreed to keep apart.

mizpeh.title: Mizpeh
mizpeh.note: Another spelling of Mizpah, the watchpost name given to several places in Israel.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nabal.title: Nabal
nabal.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nabal.note: A rich, hard man. David's men had guarded his shepherds, and when David asked for food Nabal sent back insults. Only his wife Abigail, riding out with a generous gift, kept David from killing his whole household. When she told Nabal ten days later what he had nearly brought on them, he seems to have had a stroke, and he died. David married Abigail.

nahash.title: Nahash
nahash.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash.note: The Ammonite king who besieged Jabesh-gilead and offered peace only if he could put out every man's right eye. That threat rallied Israel behind Saul, newly anointed, for his first victory.

naioth.title: Naioth
naioth.note: Near Ramah, apparently a cluster of houses where Samuel kept his company of prophets. David ran there from Saul. Saul's messengers arrived and fell to prophesying, then Saul came himself and did the same, and David got away.

ner.title: Ner
ner.about: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
ner.note: Father of Abner, Saul's army commander. Ner was Saul's grandfather or great-uncle, depending on how the genealogies are fitted together.

nob.title: Nob
nob.note: A town of priests near Jerusalem. David came here running from Saul, and the priest Ahimelech gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Saul had the priests of Nob killed for it.

ophrah-2.title: Ophrah
ophrah-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

palti.title: Palti
palti.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
palti.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

paran.title: Paran
paran.note: Ishmael grew up in this wilderness after Hagar was sent away with him, and Israel camped there for part of the long march.

peninnah.title: Peninnah
peninnah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
peninnah.note: Elkanah's other wife. She had children while Hannah had none, and she taunted Hannah about it year after year, until Hannah's grief drove her to pray at Shiloh.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phinehas-2.title: Phinehas
phinehas-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
phinehas-2.note: One of Eli's corrupt sons, killed in battle on the same day the Philistines captured the Ark of the Covenant.

rachal.title: Rachal
rachal.note: David sent a share of the plunder from his Amalekite raid to the elders here, a town in Judah's Negev. Nobody has located it.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramathaimzophim.title: Ramathaimzophim
ramathaimzophim.note: The fuller form of Ramah, Samuel's hometown in the hill country of Ephraim. The "Zophim" part ties it to the clan of Zuph, his family.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

sechu.title: Sechu
sechu.note: Saul stopped at the great well here and asked where Samuel and David were. It lay between Gibeah and Ramah, and the site has not been identified.

sela-hammalekoth.title: Sela-hammalekoth
sela-hammalekoth.note: Saul and David were on opposite sides of this mountain in the wilderness of Maon, and Saul was closing in. Then a messenger came with word of the Philistines, and Saul turned back. The name means rock of escape.

seneh.title: Seneh
seneh.note: The rocky cliff on the south side of the pass at Michmash, facing the crag called Bozez. Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed it to attack a Philistine garrison.

shaaraim.title: Shaaraim
shaaraim.note: The name means two gates. When David killed Goliath, the Philistines fled along the road past this Shaaraim, out in the Shephelah.

shalim.title: Shalim
shalim.note: Saul came through the land of Shalim while he was hunting for his father's stray donkeys, before he was anointed king. Where exactly it lay is uncertain.

shalisha.title: Shalisha
shalisha.note: Saul passed through here looking for the lost donkeys too. The name means triple land, and the route puts it in the hill country of Ephraim.

shammah.title: Shammah
shammah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shammah.note: Genesis 36 has a Shammah among its chiefs, and 1 Samuel 16:9 and 17:13 name one as a brother of David. The name was used more than once.

shen.title: Shen
shen.note: A landmark, apparently a rock or ridge, between Mizpah and Jeshanah. After the Philistines were beaten in 1 Samuel 7, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

shual-2.title: Shual
shual-2.note: The land of Shual was a district in Benjamin's hill country. Philistine raiders went through it in Saul's reign.

shunem.title: Shunem
shunem.note: A village of Issachar near Jezreel. The Philistines camped here before the battle on Mount Gilboa where Saul and his sons died, and a woman here built a room for Elisha.

shur.title: Shur
shur.note: The wilderness on Egypt's northeastern frontier, between Egypt and Philistia. The name probably comes from a wall the Egyptians built there against raiders. Hagar ran toward it when Sarah sent her away.

siphmoth.title: Siphmoth
siphmoth.note: After David took back the plunder from an Amalekite raid, he sent a share to the elders of Judah in the Negev towns where he had been sheltered as a fugitive. Siphmoth was one of those towns.

sisera.title: Sisera
sisera.about: Deborah's adversary living before Israel's Monarchy
sisera.note: He commanded the Canaanite army that held Israel down for twenty years, until Deborah and Barak beat it. Sisera ran on foot to the tent of a woman called Jael, who took him in and then killed him.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

telaim.title: Telaim
telaim.note: Saul gathered his army here before he went against the Amalekites, in the Negev of Judah. It is probably the Telem of Joshua 15:24.

tohu.title: Tohu
tohu.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
tohu.note: Several generations back in Samuel's family line, before his father Elkanah.

urim.title: Urim
urim.note: The Urim and Thummim sat in the high priest's breastpiece. They were used to put yes-or-no questions to God. How they actually worked, nobody knows.

zelzah.title: Zelzah
zelzah.note: It was a landmark in the sign Samuel gave Saul, a place near Rachel's tomb on the border of Benjamin.

zeruiah.title: Zeruiah
zeruiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
zeruiah.note: David's sister, the mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel. David said the sons of Zeruiah were too much for him.

ziklag.title: Ziklag
ziklag.note: Achish of Gath gave this town in the Negev to David while he was running from Saul, and David lived there more than a year. Amalekites burned it while he was away and took the women and children, and he went after them and got everyone back.

ziph.title: Ziph
ziph.note: David hid in the wilderness around Ziph, southeast of Hebron, while Saul was hunting him. The people of Ziph told Saul where he was, twice.

ziphim.title: Ziphim
ziphim.note: The people of Ziph, who twice gave David's hiding place away to Saul. Psalm 54 is headed with that betrayal.

zoba.title: Zoba
zoba.note: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. Saul fought it, David beat its king Hadadezer and took his chariots and his bronze, and a man from Zobah named Rezon troubled Solomon from Damascus.

zophai.title: Zophai
zophai.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
zophai.note: He was a Kohathite Levite and Samuel's ancestor, also spelled Zuph. The hill country where Elkanah's family lived was called the land of Zuph after him.

zophai-2.title: Zophai
zophai-2.note: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.
